Beállítom Drón csapódott be egy dél-orosz strandon, az esetben hét ember, köztük három gyerek halt meg – írja a BBC orosz források alapján. Az eset a Krasznodari határterület régiójában történt, a Fekete-tenger partján, Gelendzsik üdülővárosban. A terület kormányzója, Venyiamin Kondratyjev szerint összesen negyvenen sérültek meg, tizenheten kórházba kerültek. Ukrajna egyelőre még nem kommentálta az esetet. A BBC cikke szerint nem egyértelmű, hogy mi okozta a becsapódást. Ukrán Telegram-csatornákon az a hír terjed, hogy a drón azért zuhant le, mert oroszok zavarták a jeleit. Orosz források szerint a becsapódás előtt lövések dördültek el, ami azt is jelentheti, hogy megpróbálták orosz katonák lelőni a szerkezetet. A Reuters szerint Kondratyjev is egy korábbi nyilatkozatában arról beszélt, hogy drónalkatrészek zuhantak le a strandon. A helyiek nem hallottak légitámadásra utaló szirénákat. Ukrajna és Oroszország is azt állítja, hogy nem támadnak meg szándékosan civileket a több mint négy éve tartó háborúban. Ukrajna július végén a legnagyobb orosz online kereskedő, a Wildberries raktárait támadta drónokkal Volgográdban, Tatárföldön és Udmurtföldön. Gelendzsik közelében található az a luxuskomplexum, amit Putyin kastélyaként is emlegetnek. Tavaly ott egy lezuhant drón okozott erdőtüzet . https://www.dw.com/en/pakistan-islamabad.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5JOEK The fire was believed to have been caused by a malfunctioning air conditioning unit Image: Akhtar Soomro/REUTERS Advertisement A least 14 infants were killed after a fire broke out at the maternity ward of a hospital in Islamabad, Pakistan , on Wednesday. "A fire broke out on the third floor of the MCH Ward at PIMS Hospital," the district office of Islamabad said, referring to the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences. The blaze broke out at around 6:45 a.m. (0145 UTC) when an air conditioning unit exploded inside the nursery, rescuers said. Distraught parents gathered outside the hospital Image: Aamir Qureshi/AFP Officials said 16 newborns were in the ward at the time, adding that one was rescued. Outside the hospital, a nurse read out the names of babies who had perished as their families gathered around. "I lost my daughter. She was only three days old," one father told the AFP news agency. "My wife was in the ward. They took everyone out. We were sitting on the road waiting for help." Investigation underway Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif has ordered an immediate investigation into the incident. "A tragedy involving children is an irreparable loss," he said in a statement. "Those ​responsible should be identified, and ​the strictest action should be taken." The incident is one of the deadliest hospital fires in recent memory in Pakistan, where healthcare is subsidized but public hospitals are often are under-resourced and overburdened. Ambassadors from the EU’s 27 member states failed to reach agreement at a meeting early on Tuesday – their third session in around 24 hours on the topic. The senior diplomats will reconvene later today just hours ahead of a legal deadline. Without an agreement sanctions on nearly 3,000 people and entities accused of supporting the war on Ukraine will lapse at the end of Tuesday 22 September. The list includes Vladimir Putin, foreign minister Sergei Lavrov, Duma deputies, Russia’s major banks, energy companies and military industrial complex. https://news.antiwar.com/2026/10/06/lith.text: Lithuania Moves To Lift Nuclear Weapons Ban as Trump Considers Permanent US Base Lithuania’s parliament on Tuesday took the first step toward lifting a ban on the deployment of nuclear weapons in its territory, a move that comes after President Trump said he’s considering establishing a permanent US military base in the country. One hundred and six members of Lithuania’s 141-seat unicameral parliament, the Seimas, voted to advance a constitutional amendment that would repeal a ban on weapons of mass destruction and foreign military bases in Lithuania. A second vote is needed to advance the amendment, and that will be held on January 12, 2027. At least 94 members of the Seimas must support it for the change to be made. Lithuanian President Gitanas Nauseda announced in July that he was initiating an amendment to repeal the ban, outlined in Article 137 of the Lithuanian Constitution, and said the idea has “practically unanimous” support in the Seimas. Nauseda and other proponents of repealing the ban say it’s needed for Lithuania to fully participate in NATO’s “nuclear deterrence.” The move will open up Lithuania to potentially host US nuclear weapons under NATO’s nuclear sharing program, under which the US has nukes deployed in Germany, Italy, Belgium, the Netherlands, and Turkey. Lithuania’s move comes after Finland, which, like Lithuania, shares a border with Russia, lifted its prohibition on nuclear weapons . Russia strongly condemned both moves and has warned it will respond. “Neither of these developments will contribute to stability and predictability on the European continent,” Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said on Tuesday, referring to Lithuania’s parliament voting to repeal both the ban on nuclear weapons and foreign military bases. “On the contrary, they will, to our regret, mark yet another significant escalation of tensions. As for Russia, of course, Moscow will be forced to take all necessary measures to guarantee its own security,” Peskov added. The US has troops deployed in Lithuania on a rotational basis but doesn’t have a permanent base in the country, something Lithuanian Prime Minister Mindaugas Sinkevičius has said the country is willing to fund. When asked about the proposal, President Trump said he would consider it. “They’re friends of mine; they’re great people, so we’ll certainly look at it.
